known_bad.what: CARRIED UNCHANGED FROM rc1 AND STILL LIVE. Every published stream in this project carries an Artifactory property named `layout.canonical_hash`, written by scripts/ci/gds_canonical_hash.py. The name reads like a layout identity and the value cannot support that reading: measured 2026-08-26, KLayout strmxor 0.30.10 reported NO DIFFERENCES between two streams across all 49 layer/datatype pairs while their canonical hashes DIFFERED at identical byte count (302,688,050) and identical record count (34,791,830), because write_stream is not order-deterministic. rc2 gives that its own corroboration without an XOR: outputs/nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_rc2.gds (md5 0b72b1301f2087f943bb0c3dabcb2731) and outputs/nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_rc2v3r4ctl.gds (md5 9769ede7851d5bd466c1f06102e8306d) are two write_stream invocations of the same unedited geometry, identical in size at 309,421,274 bytes and different in md5.
known_bad.decision: NOT withdrawn and NOT rewritten. The digest is correct for what it computes and the raw md5/sha256 beside it are load-bearing -- a foundry Final Report cites the md5. What is wrong is the DIRECTION a reader may take from it, so gds_canonical_hash.py now returns a `claim` field saying a MATCH implies the same layout and a MISMATCH implies nothing, and the layout question is answered separately by scripts/ci/gds_xor_arbiter.py. NOTE FOR THIS CANDIDATE: that arbiter has no reference to run against here (see `supersedes`), so on rc2 the canonical hash is the ONLY digest-shaped thing in the record and the temptation to read it as a layout answer is correspondingly larger.
known_bad.withdraw_when: the store stops publishing this digest under a `layout.*` name -- either renamed to something that says RECORD SEQUENCE, or accompanied by the gds-layout-identity gate's verdict as a sibling property. Until then, treat a `layout.canonical_hash` mismatch as a prompt to run the arbiter and never as a finding.

rc1's upf-power-intent gate FAILED and rc2 has no CLP run at all, so on rc2 the same row will read NOT-MEASURED. THE FAILURE HAS NOT GONE AWAY. rc1's measurement, from build/gdsrun-20260826-rc1-clp/{cpf,upf}/clp_manifest.txt: the CPF elaborates and checks run and it carries 138 error-severity Conformal Low Power violations over 3 rules (ISO7=64, PDM1=72, PG_CON1=2); the UPF is worse in the way that matters -- intent_elaborated=no, checks_ran=no -- so its smaller violation count is an elaboration failure, not a cleaner design. THE INPUT IS UNCHANGED: both runs read build/gdsrun-20260826-rc1/outputs/nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_gate_power.v, whose md5 is still 4f0043247e0088ccd651f1f1dd899502 as re-verified on 2026-08-27, and rc2 does not re-synthesise, so it emits no power intent and no gate netlist of its own. The 138 violations are as true of rc2's design as of rc1's.
  WHY THE GATE CANNOT SAY SO. gate_upf_power_intent requires the CLP run's `netlist` to sit under spec.base_run/outputs, and rc2's base_run is its own build directory, whose outputs/ holds only P&R netlists. Pointing clp_runs at the rc1 tree would produce exactly that refusal with a correct reason; naming nothing produces a refusal with a vaguer one. Neither is a pass and this entry is the record of which.
known_bad.decision: CARRIED AS AN INHERITED FAIL. Do not read rc2's NOT-MEASURED CLP row as an improvement on rc1's FAIL. The cheap fix before publishing is to re-run `ASIC/genus-innovus/scripts/conformal/run_clp.sh` against a build whose outputs/ holds the gate netlist, or to record the rc1 result explicitly as this entry does. The underlying UPF elaboration failure is a separate open item and is not made better by either.
known_bad.withdraw_when: a Conformal Low Power run reports 0 error-severity violations with intent_elaborated=yes and checks_ran=yes on BOTH the CPF and the UPF emitted for the netlist behind this stream. A run that elaborates neither, or one whose violation count merely falls because the intent stopped compiling, does not withdraw it.

known_bad.what: CLOSED ON rc4. On rc3fix this was the last open timing debt: one setup endpoint at the signoff corner (SS/1.08V/125C, 125C RC extraction) at WNS -0.001, TNS -0.001, FEP 1 of 68,303. rc4 reads setup +0.015 / 0.000 / 0 at the same corner, in the same Tempus run that reads hold +0.003 / 0.000 / 0. HOW: three cell resizes on the ONE contended net, applied by ECO and read back from the database after place_eco, route_eco, re-fill and fix_drc (final.resizes_verified = 3/3): u_..._u_tidelink/g57706 FA1D0->FA1D1, u_..._u_soc/g127940 ND2D3->CKND2D3, u_..._u_tidelink/g33463 OAI21D1->OAI21D2. Netlist diff is exactly 3 lines. AN EARLIER READING OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: the claim that '~13 ps had to be allocated between setup and hold' was an artefact of a GLOBAL hold_target_slack sweep. The contention was one net, not the design; three local resizes recovered the setup with hold measurably untouched at all three views.
known_bad.decision: WITHDRAWN as a debt. rc4 needs no frequency de-rating: it closes at the declared 100.00 MHz. The reasons rc3fix was shippable at 99.99 MHz still hold and are no longer needed. NOTE what did NOT change: the derate factors remain the stated engineering assumption recorded under known_bad[hold-fep], and both checks remain CPPR-financed -- with CPPR off this design reads setup -0.154 and hold -0.605. rc4 improves the margin inside that assumption; it does not retire the assumption.
known_bad.withdraw_when: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-29 on rc4. Re-open only if a re-run at the signoff corner reads FEP > 0.

known_bad.what:
Voltus static rail on rc3fix's own database answers the question LVS on this design was structurally incapable of answering. instances_analysed 367,244 of 367,737 in the database -- the +1,504 ECO cells are ALL analysed and ALL reached. iv_disconnected_functional = 0. The 18 disconnected instances are FILL/DCAP endcaps in one contiguous pre-existing island, IDENTICAL in count to rc2, with zero logic cells. The 493 instances outside the analysis are the IO ring (VDDIO/VSSIO excluded by name), name-for-name the same as rc2's.
  NOT RE-RUN ON rc4. The last rail measurement is on rc3fix (ASIC/genus-innovus/rail/work/rc3fix-20260829). rc4 differs from rc3fix by three cell resizes and a re-fill, so this result is CARRIED FORWARD BY ARGUMENT, not re-measured: two of the three resizes step drive strength up by one, which raises local current draw slightly. The direction of the error is therefore known and adverse, and the margin it eats is unquantified. See not_measured[rail-not-rerun-on-rc4].
known_bad.decision: This is EVIDENCE, recorded here because it is the only power-connectivity evidence that exists for any candidate. It matters because before commit 77f06a2 this project's LVS could not detect a stranded PG pin at all -- its sign was inverted, and breaking a ground pin made LVS cleaner. SCOPE, stated: static at assumed activity, techonly PGV so cell internals are not modelled, die-only with no package model, and the IO ring is not analysed at all -- nothing in this project establishes that any IO cell reaches a VDDIO/VSSIO pad.
known_bad.withdraw_when: not a defect - this entry records a measurement and is withdrawn only if superseded by a rail run on a later database.

not_measured.asserts: that every timing check in the design was evaluated
not_measured.why: 57,955 timing checks are UNTESTED in rc4's signoff run and sta_gate.py FAILS on them. THIS IS NOT AN rc4 REGRESSION: the number is IDENTICAL -- 57,955 -- in rc2's sta_final and rc3fix's sta_final6. Breakdown: PulseWidth 49,466/169,356; Library Clock Gating Setup 3,007/6,014; Recovery 2,998/43,284; Setup 2,377/68,303. VIOLATED IS ZERO IN EVERY CATEGORY. The untested set looks structural rather than directional: the SAME counts appear in both directions (Setup 2,377 and Hold 2,377; Library Clock Gating Setup 3,007 and Hold 3,007; Recovery 2,998 and Removal 2,998), which is the signature of one set of endpoints excluded from timing altogether -- unclocked, constant-tied or case-analysis-disabled -- not of an analysis that ran one way and not the other. The tied-off SE with no scan chain is a plausible contributor and has NOT been confirmed. Nobody has enumerated these endpoints. Until someone does, 'setup and hold close' means 'over the 96% of checks that were evaluated'.

not_measured.asserts: IR drop and electromigration on the stream being submitted
not_measured.why: The Voltus static rail run is on rc3fix, not rc4. rc4 adds three up-sized cells and a re-fill. Both known_bad rail rows (49 EM elements over the derated limit, worst J/Jmax 1.437; worst IR collapse 1.336% against a 1.0% budget) are carried forward by argument. Two of the three resizes increase drive strength, so the carried numbers are optimistic by an unmeasured amount. A rail re-run on rc4-20260829/db_rc4 would close this and takes roughly the same wall time as the rc3fix run.
